Randomization ratio of blinded data pooled from several studies

Source: R/pooled_ratio.R
pooled_ratio.Rd

Computes the effective randomization ratio of study drug to control for blinded data pooled from studies with different randomization ratios, as described by Waterhouse et al. (2022, Appendix A). The pooled numbers of events and the pooled exposure can then be analyzed with bdribs_post and this ratio as k.

Usage

pooled_ratio(exposure, k)

Arguments

exposure

Exposures of the studies (positive).

k

Randomization ratios of the studies (study drug to control).

Value

The pooled randomization ratio.

Details

Study \(j\) with exposure \(E_j\) and randomization ratio \(k_j\) contributes the expected exposures \(E_j k_j / (k_j + 1)\) on study drug and \(E_j / (k_j + 1)\) on control. The pooled ratio is the ratio of the totals, $$k = \sum_j E_j k_j / (k_j + 1) \Big/ \sum_j E_j / (k_j + 1).$$

References

Waterhouse, B., Hartford, A., Mukhopadhyay, S., Ferguson, R. and Hendrickson, B. A. (2022). Using the Bayesian detection of potential risk using inference on blinded safety data (BDRIBS) method to support the decision to refer an event for unblinded evaluation. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 21(2), 372–385. doi:10.1002/pst.2175

See also

bdribs_post, bdribs_grid

Examples

# Example 3 of Waterhouse et al. (2022): 250 patient-years at 1:1 and
# 80 patient-years at 2:1
k <- pooled_ratio(c(250, 80), c(1, 2))
k
#> [1] 1.175824
bdribs_post(y = 16, exposure = 330, k = k, lambda_hp = 0.031, pt_hp = Inf)
#> Model: BDRIBS 
#> Relative risk: rate ratio r of study drug to placebo
#> P(r > 1 | data) = 0.9101
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no
#> Posterior of r: mean 1.905, median 1.846, 95% interval (0.6727, 3.469)
